- "Most" implies more than half of the 20 trains, so at least 11 high-speed trains. However, the options must align with the phrasing of "some motor trains" and "hardly any ordinary fast trains."
- "Some motor trains" typically suggests a small but non-zero number, usually more than one (e.g., 2–4). "Hardly any ordinary fast trains" implies the number of ordinary trains is negligible (likely 0 or 1).
- If ordinary trains are 0, then motor trains and high-speed trains sum to 20. If motor trains are "some" (e.g., 2), then high-speed trains would be 18. If motor trains were 1, "some" might not fit the common interpretation (as "some" often implies more than one), making 19 less plausible.
- Option A (10) is invalid because "most" requires more than half (i.e., >10). Option C (20) is impossible because there are "some motor trains," meaning not all are high-speed. Option B (19) would imply only 1 motor train, which may not satisfy "some" (as "some" usually implies multiple).

Given the constraints, the most reasonable guess is 18 high-speed trains, as it allows for "some" motor trains (e.g., 2) and "hardly any ordinary" (0), fitting the narrative logically.
